current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024-2026 (193rd/194th General Court). Primary sources: owner-supplied official text of M.G.L. c. 66, s. 10 (malegislature.gov, fetched 2026-08-20, complete subsections (a)-(f)) and 950 CMR 32.00 (Public Records Access, Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth, complete 32.01-32.10; Mass. Register #1445, 6/11/21 stamp on 32.02). Currency check (web): malegislature.gov prints no history line; FindLaw shows c. 66 s. 10 current as of Jan. 1, 2025 with the same text; 2025 session laws located (e.g., Acts of 2025, c. 16, s. 5, eff. 11/5/2025) amend c. 66 s. 10B (personal-information protections for reproductive/gender-affirming care and public-safety personnel), NOT s. 10; no 2024-2026 amendment to the s. 10 fee provisions was found. The fee section stands as rewritten by the 2016 reform (St. 2016, c. 121, eff. 1/1/2017). Guidance-vs-law gap: none material for fees; 950 CMR 32.07 tracks the statute and adds operative detail (no fee for electronic/fax copies; postage rules; small-municipality first-2-hours charging with census burden; fee-rights waiver on petition noncompliance).

resolutions.unit: USD per page (single- or double-sided, B&W paper copies/printouts)
resolutions.source_language: the fee assessed for standard black and white paper copies or printouts of records shall not exceed 5 cents per page, for both single and double-sided black and white copies or printouts
resolutions.notes: Ceiling under a Permission (§ 10(d): RAO 'may assess a reasonable fee'); city sets its operative rate at or under $0.05. Regulation extends the same cap to B&W copies 'of any size susceptible to ordinary means of production' (MA-9001). Overall bound: fee shall not exceed actual cost of reproducing the record (MA-0029).

resolutions.source_language: A records access officer may assess a reasonable fee for the production of a public record except those records that are freely available for public inspection. The reasonable fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record.
resolutions.manual_verification: Confirm treatment of color copies: the 5-cent cap is expressly limited to 'black and white' copies; color is left to the general reasonable-fee/actual-cost ceiling. Scope judgment, not an express color provision.
resolutions.notes: The prior snippet's 5-cent figure belongs to the B&W item only — § 10(d)(i) and 950 CMR 32.07(2)(e) both say 'black and white'. No color-specific rate exists; color copies fall under the general standard: reasonable fee not to exceed actual cost of reproduction.

resolutions.source_language: for copies of public records not susceptible to ordinary means of reproduction, the actual cost incurred in providing a copy may be assessed.
resolutions.notes: Two-branch rule: an oversized B&W page still 'susceptible to ordinary means of production' is capped at $0.05/page 'of any size' (32.07(2)(e), MA-9001); a copy NOT susceptible to ordinary means of reproduction may be charged at actual cost incurred (32.07(2)(h), MA-9002). No fixed oversized rate exists.

resolutions.source_language: for copies of public records not susceptible to ordinary means of reproduction, the actual cost incurred in providing a copy may be assessed.
resolutions.notes: Specialty reproduction (photographs, maps, and similar non-ordinary media) is governed by the actual-cost-incurred standard of 32.07(2)(h); no per-item schedule. Storage device/material also at actual cost (MA-0031). No transcription-specific fee provision in c. 66 § 10 or 950 CMR 32.00.

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10(d)(i)-(ix) and 950 CMR 32.07 read — the per-page cap is flat ($0.05 at any volume); no graduated page bands exist. The prior's '2 hours'/'4 hours' figures are the free-LABOR-hour thresholds, not page tiers; the machine-derived value_present status was a mis-join.

No free-PAGE allowance exists (the free allowance is stated in labor hours — see rules.freeLaborHours). Material adjacent rule captured as MA-9003: no copying fee may be assessed at all for electronic copies or copies transmitted by facsimile (950 CMR 32.07(2)(f)) — a no-charge category, not a page allowance. The prior's 2/4-hour values are labor thresholds, not pages.

resolutions.unit: USD per hour (and not more than the hourly rate of the lowest-paid employee with the necessary skill)
resolutions.source_language: if a municipality is required to devote more than 2 hours of employee time to search for, compile, segregate, redact or reproduce a record requested, the records access officer may include as part of the fee an hourly rate equal to or less than the hourly rate attributed to the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill required to search for, compile, segregate, redact or reproduce the record requested but the fee (A) shall not be more than $25 per hour unless such rate is approved by the supervisor of records under clause (iv)
resolutions.notes: Municipal double ceiling: lower of $25/hr and the lowest-paid capable employee's hourly rate; a municipality (only) may exceed $25/hr with Supervisor of Records approval under § 10(d)(iv) (MA-0037). Agency regime (noted): same structure with a 4-hour trigger and a hard $25 cap with no exceedance path (§ 10(d)(ii), MA-0033). Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.07(2)(i), (m)3.

resolutions.unit: USD per hour (when chargeable at all)
resolutions.source_language: (C) shall not be assessed for time spent segregating or redacting records unless such segregation or redaction is required by law or approved by the supervisor of records under clause (iv)
resolutions.notes: Default: segregation/redaction time is NOT chargeable at all unless (a) the segregation/redaction is required by law, or (b) the Supervisor of Records approves a petition (§ 10(d)(iv), MA-0037). When chargeable, it sits inside the same municipal labor ceiling ($25/hr / lowest-paid capable employee, MA-0032). Reg parallels: 950 CMR 32.07(2)(d), (m)4.

resolutions.source_language: As used in this section, ''employee time'' means time required by employees or necessary vendors, including outside legal counsel, technology and payroll consultants or others as needed by the municipality.
resolutions.notes: No separate programming/data-extraction rate: 'compile ... or reproduce' labor is billed under the single municipal labor ceiling (MA-0032), and § 10(f) expressly folds necessary VENDOR time (technology consultants, outside counsel) into 'employee time' (new row MA-9004) — so extraction work by an IT vendor is still subject to the $25/hr / lowest-paid-capable-employee ceiling absent Supervisor approval. Note 950 CMR 32.07(1)(f): furnishing a segregable portion/extract of existing data is not creation of a new record.

resolutions.unit: hours of employee time devoted to the request (municipal chargeability trigger)
resolutions.source_language: if a municipality is required to devote more than 2 hours of employee time to search for, compile, segregate, redact or reproduce a record requested, the records access officer may include as part of the fee an hourly rate ... (B) shall not be assessed for the first 2 hours of work performed where the responding municipality has a population of over 20,000 people
resolutions.notes: Labor is chargeable only when the municipality must devote MORE than 2 hours of employee time (agency: 4 hours, § 10(d)(ii)). Population gate on the free tier: municipalities over 20,000 (decennial U.S. Census) may not assess the first 2 hours; municipalities of 20,000 or fewer MAY assess the first 2 hours, with the RAO bearing the burden of providing census data (950 CMR 32.07(2)(m)2, MA-9005). Not paper-only — applies to all labor categories in the clause. Segregation/redaction time separately gated (MA-0036).

resolutions.source_language: a records access officer shall assess no fee greater than the lowest hourly rate of a person capable of compiling, segregating, redacting and reproducing a requested record, subject to the requirements of 950 CMR 32.07.
resolutions.manual_verification: Categorical-preclusion reading: no MA provision authorizes an overhead/fringe multiplier, and the hourly fee is capped at the lowest-paid capable employee's rate (and $25), which leaves no room to layer a surcharge above the base wage. Confirm no Supervisor guidance permits an overhead component within the cap.
resolutions.notes: No overhead or fringe surcharge exists in MA law; the labor fee is structurally capped at the base hourly rate of the lowest-paid capable employee (§ 10(d)(iii)(A) 'an hourly rate equal to or less than the hourly rate attributed to the lowest paid employee'; reg parallel quoted). A percentage add-on above that rate cannot exist under the cap, hence not_applicable rather than silent. Exceeding $25/hr requires a § 10(d)(iv) Supervisor petition, which is a rate approval, not an overhead multiplier.

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no billing-increment or rounding rule (no quarter-hour/15-minute provision). Cities set their own increment policy under the general reasonable-fee/actual-cost ceiling.

resolutions.unit: free hours of employee time per request (municipality with population over 20,000)
resolutions.source_language: (B) shall not be assessed for the first 2 hours of work performed where the responding municipality has a population of over 20,000 people
resolutions.notes: Population-gated: 2 free hours per request applies only to municipalities over 20,000 (decennial U.S. Census); a municipality of 20,000 or fewer may assess a fee for the first two hours, bearing the burden to provide population data (950 CMR 32.07(2)(m)2, MA-9005). Agency regime (noted): 4 free hours (§ 10(d)(ii)(B), MA-0035). Per-request allowance, not per-requestor-period.

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no per-requestor per-month/per-year free personnel-time ledger (no TX § 552.275 analogue). The 2-hour/4-hour free tiers are PER REQUEST (see rules.freeLaborHours); the prior's value_present status mis-joined them to this item.

resolutions.source_language: if fees are being assessed, a records access officer shall provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate of any fees that may be charged to produce the records prior to complying with a public records request within ten business days following receipt of a request.
resolutions.notes: No dollar/hours threshold: the written, itemized, good-faith estimate is required WHENEVER any fee will be assessed (threshold effectively $0), and it must precede compliance and land within the 10-business-day response. Companion notice duty (MA-9009): the RAO shall inform the requester of records' availability online to avoid delays and fees (950 CMR 32.07(2)(a)). Statutory hook: the § 10(b) written response must 'include an itemized, good faith estimate of any fees that may be charged to produce the records'.

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no deadline for the requester to accept/respond to an estimate and no deemed-withdrawal clock. The prior's defers_to_city status overstated it: the law is silent, not an express deferral; a city response-window policy would sit in unregulated space. Nonpayment is handled instead by delay-until-paid (MA-0044) and denial for prior unpaid balances (MA-0041).

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no revised-estimate trigger at any overrun percentage. The 'good faith estimate' standard (32.07(2)(b)) is the only constraint on estimate accuracy.
Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no estimate validity/expiry period.

resolutions.source_language: a records access officer may delay provision of records until all fees related to such requests are paid in full by the person seeking access to the requested records in accordance with 950 CMR 32.07.
resolutions.notes: MA has no deposit-threshold mechanism. The state's shape is a payment GATE, not a deposit: production may be conditioned on payment of the assessed fee at any amount (§ 10(a)(iii) conditions the production duty on 'payment of a reasonable fee'; the RAO may delay provision until fees are paid in full). No dollar threshold exists above which prepayment becomes permissible — it is permissible whenever a fee is properly assessed (which itself requires the timely response, § 10(e), and the itemized estimate, 32.07(2)(b)).

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no partial-deposit concept and therefore no deposit cap percentage. The regulation instead permits withholding production until fees are paid IN FULL (32.06(2)(f)); a city adopting a partial-deposit practice operates in unregulated space under the actual-cost ceiling.

resolutions.source_language: (iii) the records access officer receives payment of a reasonable fee as set forth in subsection (d).
resolutions.notes: Gate confirmed both ways: the 10-business-day production duty is expressly conditioned on receipt of payment (§ 10(a)(iii)), and the RAO 'may delay provision of records until all fees related to such requests are paid in full' (32.06(2)(f), MA-0044). Pay-in-full-before-release model; permission (may), not requirement.

resolutions.source_language: (vi) the records access officer may deny public records requests from a requester who has failed to compensate the agency or municipality for previously produced public records; (vii) the records access officer shall provide a written notification to the requester detailing the reasons behind the denial, including an itemized list of any balances attributed to previously produced records;
resolutions.notes: No withdrawn-after-N-days rule. The nonpayment consequences are: (1) the current request may be held unreleased until paid in full (MA-0044); (2) NEW requests from a requester with unpaid prior balances may be denied — but per 950 CMR 32.07(2)(n) (MA-9006) only if the prior fee estimate complied with 950 CMR 32.00 AND the requester agreed to pay it, and the denial must be a written notice with an itemized list of the outstanding balances (§ 10(d)(vii)).

resolutions.source_language: a records access officer may delay provision of records until all fees related to such requests are paid in full by the person seeking access to the requested records in accordance with 950 CMR 32.07.
resolutions.manual_verification: Clock-effect reading is inferential: § 10(a) makes payment a proviso of the 10-business-day production duty, so the delivery obligation is suspended while a properly assessed fee is unpaid; but neither source states an express tolling rule, grace period, or lapse action. Confirm against Supervisor of Records appeal decisions if the engine needs a firm tolling semantic.
resolutions.notes: MA has no deposit clock because it has no deposit stage; the analogous effect is that production may lawfully be withheld while assessed fees are unpaid (pause-like gate on delivery). No statutory grace period and no request-lapse/withdrawal action for nonpayment of the current request — the request simply remains unfulfilled, and future requests may be denied for the unpaid balance (§ 10(d)(vi)).

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no rule requiring a revised estimate when actual cost overruns the estimate, none blocking collection of an overrun, none restarting a window. Practical bounds that survive: the fee may never exceed actual reproduction cost (MA-0029) and the estimate must have been made in good faith (32.07(2)(b)); 32.07(2)(n)1 conditions prior-debt denial on a compliant prior estimate the requester agreed to.
out of scope per owner decision 2026-08-20 — finance-department policy, excluded from state rules profile

resolutions.source_language: A records access officer may assess a reasonable fee for the production of a public record except those records that are freely available for public inspection. The reasonable fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record.
resolutions.notes: Request-level cap is the actual-cost standard: 'reasonable fee' that 'shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record' (verbatim; reg parallel 32.07(2)(c)). The itemized component ceilings ($0.05/page, $25/hr, free hours) all sit under this envelope. Records freely available for public inspection may not be charged for at all.

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no de-minimis dollar floor below which charging is barred. Adjacent no-charge categories that are NOT a de-minimis rule: freely-inspectable records (§ 10(d)), electronic/fax copies (32.07(2)(f), MA-9003), and the discretionary waiver power (MA-0038). A city may adopt its own de-minimis policy via that discretion.

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no minimum-fee provision. A flat minimum charge exceeding actual reproduction cost would collide with the actual-cost ceiling (MA-0029), so any municipal minimum must stay within actual cost.

resolutions.source_language: the actual cost of any storage device or material provided to a person in response to a request for public records under subsection (a) may be included as part of the fee
resolutions.notes: CD/DVD/USB and similar media: actual cost of the storage device or material, verbatim standard, no fixed schedule. Note the transmission itself must be free when electronic: no copying fee for electronic copies (32.07(2)(f), MA-9003) — only the physical device's actual cost is chargeable.

resolutions.source_language: a records access officer may assess the actual cost of postage to mail copies of public records, provided: 1. the requester specifically requests that records be mailed or is unable to receive copies in person; and 2. the records access officer shall charge the lowest cost available for such mailings, at the discretion of the requester.
resolutions.notes: Postage: actual cost only, only when the requester asks for mailing or cannot receive in person, and at the lowest available mailing cost (MA-9007). Electronic delivery and facsimile: no copying fee may be assessed at all (32.07(2)(f), MA-9003). No handling/processing surcharge is authorized. Electronic format is the presumed and preferred delivery (32.04(5)(d), 32.07(1)(c)).

resolutions.manual_verification: Certified-copy fees for specific municipal record classes (vital records, clerk-attested instruments) are set by separate MA fee statutes outside the Public Records Law (e.g., M.G.L. c. 262); those instruments were not in scope of the supplied source documents and were not opened. Flag for a targeted pass if the engine needs certification rates for those record classes.
resolutions.notes: The Public Records Law fee scheme (c. 66 § 10(d); 950 CMR 32.07) contains no certification or certified-copy charge. 950 CMR 32.05(1)(d)1 acknowledges 'certified copies of records' only as a class the Supervisor may except from agency reporting — not a fee rule. Silence here is silence of the records-law regime; class-specific fee statutes exist elsewhere and were not researched (out of the supplied-source scope).

resolutions.source_language: for copies of public records not susceptible to ordinary means of reproduction, the actual cost incurred in providing a copy may be assessed.
resolutions.manual_verification: Application of 32.07(2)(h) to audio/video is a scope judgment (A/V is not addressed by name anywhere in c. 66 § 10 or 950 CMR 32.00). No per-recording, per-minute, or free-minutes figures exist.
resolutions.notes: No A/V-specific schedule. Reproduction of recordings resolves through the general components: actual cost incurred for copies not susceptible to ordinary reproduction (2)(h), actual cost of the storage device (MA-0031), labor above the free-hour threshold at the capped rate (MA-0032/MA-0034), and no copying fee if delivered electronically (MA-9003).

resolutions.source_language: the supervisor of records may approve a petition from an agency or municipality to charge for time spent segregating or redacting, or a petition from a municipality to charge in excess of $25 per hour, if the supervisor of records determines that (A) the request is for a commercial purpose
resolutions.notes: No commercial surcharge percentage or separate commercial schedule. Commercial purpose (defined § 10(d)(ix), MA-0004; reg definition also covers solicitation lists, 32.02) operates structurally: (1) it is a ground for the Supervisor to approve redaction-time charging or municipal rates above $25/hr (§ 10(d)(iv)(A)); (2) purpose may be demanded only to test commercial purpose or a waiver request (§ 10(d)(viii)); (3) a primarily-commercial interest defeats the public-interest waiver ground (§ 10(d)(v)); (4) the Supervisor may deny an appeal made solely for a commercial purpose (32.08(2)(b)3).

resolutions.source_language: the records access officer may waive or reduce the amount of any fee charged under this subsection upon a showing that disclosure of a requested record is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requestor, or upon a showing that the requestor lacks the financial ability to pay the full amount of the reasonable fee
resolutions.notes: Discretionary ('may waive or reduce'), never mandatory. Grounds: (1) public-interest disclosure not primarily commercial; (2) requestor's inability to pay. Purpose statement: may be required from the requester ONLY to evaluate commercial purpose or the waiver (§ 10(d)(viii)). No waiver-specific written-denial duty or waiver-specific appeal; a denial is reviewable through the general Supervisor appeal (any noncompliance with 950 CMR 32.00, 32.08(1)(a), 90-calendar-day window). Reg variant 32.07(2)(k) restates the grounds as a three-clause or-list — duplicate of the statute, not a separate row.

resolutions.source_language: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).
resolutions.notes: Confirmed TRUE, two independent forfeiture triggers: (1) missing the 10-business-day § 10(b) response forfeits the entire fee right (§ 10(e), MA-0040; reg parallel 32.06(2)(c)); (2) failure to comply with the 950 CMR 32.06(4) petition provisions 'will result in a waiver of the right to assess fees for public records' (32.06(4)(b), new row MA-9008). Terminal clock effect on the fee entitlement.

Coverage: full text of c. 66 § 10 and 950 CMR 32.00 read — no FEE aggregation threshold and no unpaid-fee carry-forward-to-new-request pricing rule. Multiple requests from the same requestor matter only to TIME relief, not fees: undue burden from 'multiple requests from the same requestor' supports the § 10(b) extended timeframe and the § 10(c) Supervisor extension, and a frivolous/harassing series can relieve the body of the duty to furnish copies (§ 10(c)). Prior-debt denial (MA-0041/MA-9006) is a payment gate, not aggregation.

new_rules.legal_concept: Per-page cap extended to any size susceptible to ordinary production
new_rules.atomic_rule: The charge for black-and-white paper copies or printouts of records of ANY SIZE susceptible to ordinary means of production shall not exceed $0.05 per page, single- or double-sided.
new_rules.trigger: RAO provides B&W paper copies/printouts of records reproducible by ordinary means, regardless of page size.
new_rules.source_language: the charge for black and white paper copies or printouts of records of any size susceptible to ordinary means of production shall not exceed $0.05 per page, for both single and double-sided black and white copies or printouts.
new_rules.notes: Regulatory extension of the statutory § 10(d)(i) cap (MA-0030): adds 'of any size susceptible to ordinary means of production', so oversized-but-ordinary pages are inside the 5-cent cap; non-ordinary reproduction falls to MA-9002. Amends nothing; supplements MA-0030.

new_rules.legal_concept: Actual cost for copies not susceptible to ordinary reproduction
new_rules.atomic_rule: For copies of public records not susceptible to ordinary means of reproduction, the actual cost incurred in providing a copy may be assessed.
new_rules.trigger: Requested record cannot be reproduced by ordinary means (specialty/oversized/nonstandard media).
new_rules.source_language: for copies of public records not susceptible to ordinary means of reproduction, the actual cost incurred in providing a copy may be assessed.
new_rules.notes: Bound: actual cost incurred. Covers specialty reproduction (photographs, maps, A/V and other non-ordinary media). Sits under the overall actual-cost ceiling (MA-0029).

new_rules.legal_concept: No copying fee for electronic or facsimile copies
new_rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer shall not assess a copying fee for electronic copies or for copies of public records transmitted via facsimile.
new_rules.trigger: Records are provided as electronic copies or transmitted by facsimile.
new_rules.source_language: a records access officer shall not assess a copying fee for electronic copies or copies of public records transmitted via facsimile.
new_rules.notes: Prohibits the COPYING fee component for electronic/fax delivery; labor above the free-hour threshold and the actual cost of a physical storage device (MA-0031) remain chargeable. Material for the engine: electronic production zeroes the duplication line.

new_rules.atomic_rule: 'Employee time' means time required by employees or necessary vendors, including outside legal counsel, technology and payroll consultants or others as needed by the municipality.
new_rules.trigger: Labor fee is computed for a request (determines whose time counts toward the >2-hour trigger and the billable hours).
new_rules.source_language: As used in this section, ''employee time'' means time required by employees or necessary vendors, including outside legal counsel, technology and payroll consultants or others as needed by the municipality.
new_rules.notes: Definition the fee engine branches on: vendor time (e.g., IT extraction work) counts as employee time and is therefore subject to the same trigger, free hours, and rate ceiling — there is no separate uncapped vendor pass-through for labor.

new_rules.legal_concept: Small-municipality charging of the first two hours; census burden
new_rules.atomic_rule: A municipal RAO in a municipality with a population of 20,000 or fewer may assess a fee for the first two hours of time spent compiling, segregating, redacting and reproducing a requested record, provided population is determined by the decennial U.S. Census and the RAO bears the burden of providing population data in responses assessing such fees.
new_rules.trigger: Municipality of 20,000 or fewer population assesses labor fees for the first two hours.
new_rules.source_language: a municipal records access officer in a municipality with a population of 20,000 persons or fewer may assess a fee for the first two hours of time spent compiling, segregating, redacting and reproducing a requested record, provided: i. population data shall be determined by the decennial U.S. Census; and ii. it shall be the burden of the municipal records access officer to provide population data information in responses in which it seeks to assess such fees.
new_rules.notes: Complement of MA-0034's population gate: makes explicit that small municipalities may charge from hour zero, resolves the population source (decennial Census) and puts the evidentiary burden on the RAO. Supersedes nothing; refines the note on MA-0034 (which read small municipalities as 'not entitled to charge labor at all' — the regulation states the opposite: they may charge the first two hours).

new_rules.legal_concept: Conditions on denial for prior nonpayment
new_rules.atomic_rule: An RAO may deny access by written notice to a requester who failed to compensate the custodian for previously produced records only if a compliant fee estimate was prepared for the previous request and the requester agreed to pay it, and the written notice must detail the reasons for denial including an itemized list of outstanding balances.
new_rules.trigger: Requester with unpaid balances for previously produced records submits a new request.
new_rules.source_language: A records access officer may provide written notice denying access to public records to a requester who has failed to compensate the custodian for previously produced public records, provided: 1. a fee estimate for a previous request was prepared in compliance with 950 CMR 32.00 and the requester agreed to pay the previous fee; 2. the written notice details the reasons for denial, including an itemized list of any balances attributed to previously produced records.
new_rules.notes: Narrows MA-0041 (§ 10(d)(vi)): prior-debt denial requires (a) a 950-CMR-compliant estimate on the earlier request AND (b) the requester's agreement to pay it; itemized-balance notice duty mirrors § 10(d)(vii). Engine gate on the requestor ledger.

new_rules.legal_concept: Postage at actual cost, conditioned and lowest-cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: An RAO may assess the actual cost of postage to mail copies only if the requester specifically requests mailing or cannot receive copies in person, and must charge the lowest mailing cost available, at the requester's discretion.
new_rules.trigger: Copies are mailed at the requester's request or because the requester cannot receive them in person.
new_rules.source_language: a records access officer may assess the actual cost of postage to mail copies of public records, provided: 1. the requester specifically requests that records be mailed or is unable to receive copies in person; and 2. the records access officer shall charge the lowest cost available for such mailings, at the discretion of the requester.
new_rules.notes: Bound: actual postage cost, lowest available service. Two gate conditions before any postage line may appear on an invoice. No handling surcharge authorized.

new_rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer's failure to comply with the 950 CMR 32.06(4) petition provisions results in a waiver of the right to assess fees for the public records; petitions do not relieve the RAO of the 10-business-day initial-response duty.
new_rules.trigger: RAO files (or should have filed) a 32.06(4) petition for extension or fee-limit waiver and fails to comply with its provisions.
new_rules.clock_spec: terminal: fee-assessment right waived on 950 CMR 32.06(4) noncompliance
new_rules.source_language: petitions filed under 950 CMR 32.06(4) do not affect the requirement that a records access officer shall provide an initial response to a requester within ten business days following receipt of a request for public records, pursuant to 950 CMR 32.06(2)(a) or (b). Failure to comply with 950 CMR 32.06(4) will result in a waiver of the right to assess fees for public records.
new_rules.notes: Second, regulation-level forfeiture trigger alongside § 10(e) (MA-0040): procedural noncompliance with the petition rules costs the body its fee entitlement. Terminal effect on the fee right, like MA-0040.

new_rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer shall inform a requester of the availability of records online to avoid delays and fees associated with the provision of public records.
new_rules.source_language: A records access officer shall inform a requester of the availability of records online to avoid delays and fees associated with the provision of public records.
new_rules.notes: Mandatory fee-avoidance notice: a required communication step before charging for records that are posted online. Pairs with the itemized-estimate duty (MA-0039).

delegations_followed.statute_cite: M.G.L. c. 66, § 1 (Supervisor/Secretary regulatory authority; fee detail legislated directly in c. 66, § 10(d))
delegations_followed.instrument: 950 CMR 32.00, Public Records Access (Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth), fee section 32.07
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: $0.05/page any-size ordinary-production B&W cap (32.07(2)(e)); $25/hr municipal cap subject to Supervisor waiver (32.07(2)(m)3); 2 free hours >20,000 population / chargeable first 2 hours at <=20,000 with census burden (32.07(2)(m)1-2); no copying fee for electronic/fax copies (32.07(2)(f)); postage actual-cost-lowest-rate conditions (32.07(2)(j)); estimate-before-compliance within 10 business days (32.07(2)(b)); prior-debt denial conditions (32.07(2)(n)); fee-rights waiver on 32.06(4) noncompliance (32.06(4)(b)); delay production until paid in full (32.06(2)(f))

applicability_notes: MA runs a single statute with paired agency/municipal clauses inside § 10(d): agency labor trigger 4 hours with a hard $25/hr cap (§ 10(d)(ii)); municipal trigger 2 hours with a $25/hr cap exceedable only by Supervisor-approved petition (§ 10(d)(iii)-(iv)). All municipal resolutions here use the (iii) regime; the agency variant is noted per row.

The 2-free-hour tier is population-gated: only municipalities over 20,000 (decennial U.S. Census) must give it; municipalities of 20,000 or fewer may charge from the first hour, with the RAO bearing the burden of producing census data (950 CMR 32.07(2)(m)2).
950 CMR 32.02 'Municipality' includes cities, towns, and local housing/redevelopment authorities, plus consortia/combinations of political subdivisions — broader than cities alone.
The copy-rate, storage-device, actual-cost, estimate, payment-gate, waiver, and forfeiture rules apply to agencies and municipalities alike (all_public_bodies).
950 CMR 32.05(1) (reporting, website-posting of record categories) is agency-only and does not bind municipalities; it was not used to resolve any item.
material_negatives: No graduated per-page volume tiers — the $0.05 cap is flat at any volume (c. 66 § 10(d)(i); 950 CMR 32.07(2)(e)).
No free-page allowance; the free allowance is expressed in labor hours only.
No overhead/fringe multiplier on labor — the fee is capped at the lowest-paid capable employee's base hourly rate and $25.
No per-requestor periodic free-time ledger (no TX § 552.275 analogue).
No requester response window for estimates, no revision-percent trigger, no estimate validity period.
No deposit threshold or deposit cap percentage — the mechanism is delay-until-paid-in-full, not deposits.
No overrun re-issue rule; only the good-faith-estimate standard and the actual-cost ceiling bound overruns.
No de-minimis floor and no minimum fee.
No certification charge within the Public Records Law regime (class-specific fee statutes, e.g. M.G.L. c. 262, not researched — outside supplied sources).
No A/V per-recording/per-minute schedule and no free-minutes allowance.
No commercial surcharge schedule — commercial purpose is a classification gate, not a price.
No fee-aggregation threshold or repeat-request carry-forward pricing rule.
gaps_manual_verification: dup.color.rate: color copies resolved to the general actual-cost standard by negative implication from the express 'black and white' limitation — confirm no Supervisor guidance sets a color rate.
labor.overheadPct: not_applicable rests on the structural cap at the base wage rate; confirm no Supervisor of Records determination has permitted an overhead component within the cap.
payment.depositClock: the pause-like effect on the production duty while fees are unpaid is inferred from the § 10(a)(iii) proviso plus 32.06(2)(f); no express tolling/grace/lapse language exists.

certification: certified-copy fees for specific municipal record classes live in separate fee statutes (e.g., M.G.L. c. 262) not covered by the supplied source documents; targeted pass needed if those rates matter to the engine.
av: application of 950 CMR 32.07(2)(h) actual-cost to audio/video is a scope judgment; A/V is never named in the statute or regulation.

Currency of 950 CMR 32.00: the supplied text carries a Mass. Register #1445 (6/11/21) stamp; no later amendment was found in the 2024-2026 check, but mass.gov's regulation page should be re-confirmed at verify.
